item.title: Aberdeen sack Robinson after league slump
item.description: Stephen Robinson's Aberdeen reign is over inside eight months, with the head coach sacked after winning just three from 12 Premiership matches this season. The Dons sit second bottom and Saturday's 4-0 home defeat by Hibernian was their fourth straight loss in all competitions. Brian Kerr and Stephen Craigan have also left the club, with Stuart Duff placed in interim charge. Club hero Willie Miller described Saturday's result as "utterly embarrassing", going on to tell BBC Sportsound listeners that Robinson resembled "a man lost". The 51-year-old former Northern Ireland international previously managed Oldham Athletic, Motherwell, Morecambe and St Mirren. On the back of three successive top-six finishes and a League Cup triumph, Robinson left the Paisley side for Aberdeen in March, agreeing a contract until the summer of 2029. The sixth permanent manager since Dave Cormack took control at Pittodrie in November 2019, he steered the Dons away from relegation trouble last term before overhauling the squad with 15 signings. Across 28 games in all competitions, Robinson departs with a record of 11 wins, five draws and 12 defeats. [SNS] 'Players not up to this level' The next manager will inherit a squad low on confidence, the joint lowest scorers in the league. Robinson chopped and changed between four and five at the back but that yielded just two top-flight clean sheets. Of the plethora of summer recruits, only goalkeeper Marius Muller and full-back Nesta Guinness-Walker have played in every league game. Top scorer Kevin Nisbet is the other player to have done the same and scunnered fans cheered when the captain was replaced at the weekend. "The players aren't up to scratch, not up to playing at this level and dealing with high-ish expectations," was the damning assessment from Miller. "I'm not talking about trophies, I'm talking about being in the top six and they're nowhere near that." After the international break, Aberdeen travel to face Kilmarnock on 21 November then visit Rangers three days later before their next home game against Dundee on 28 November. item.title: 8 takeaways from the Bears' stressful win over the Buccaneers
item.description: The victories seemed to be coming a little too easy for the Chicago Bears in recent weeks, so they made sure to put everyone through an extremely stressful one before heading off for their bye week. The Bears wrapped up their three-game prime-time tour with a home matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football and escaped with a 27-24 victory and improved to 7-2 on the season. Early on, however, it felt as if the game would be a blowout. Quarterback Caleb Williams quickly led two scoring drives to put the Bears up 14-0, with Tampa seemingly having no answers on either side of the ball. Everything was looking great, but then Williams began turning the ball over, something that is rare for him. Williams threw a career-high four interceptions on the day, and the Bears had five turnovers on the day. The offense couldn't muster any momentum, putting all the pressure on the Bears defense, which came through multiple times. The defense couldn't hold their ground forever, though. Eventually, those offensive miscues helped Tampa get back into the game as the Bears blew a 24-13 lead early in the fourth quarter to be tied 24-24 with just under two minutes to play. Fortunately, Williams responded by putting together one last scoring drive, complete with a big 38-yard completion to Colston Loveland to put the Bears in field goal range. Cairo Santos drilled a game-winning kick as everyone collectively exhaled. This will be one of the more memorable wins for all the wrong reasons, but it's still a win that keeps the Bears near the top of the playoff picture. Here are our takeaways from Sunday's stressful victory: 1. This is the reincarnation of 2006's Miracle in the Desert 20 years ago, Bears fans were treated to one of the most improbable and ugly wins in a special season. That, of course, was the "Miracle in the Desert" comeback win against the Arizona Cardinals, where the Bears committed six turnovers and needed big plays from the defense and special teams to get back in the game. And though this game may not have had the same comeback theatrics, it was every bit as gross and gritty to keep the winning streak alive. For nearly three full quarters, the offense didn't do much of anything and needed to rely on big plays by the defense to pick up the slack. It was ugly, and everything that could go wrong did go wrong. But the Bears never gave up and dug deep to get this victory. And great teams need to do that every once in a while. The Miracle in the Desert proved to everyone in the locker room that they have what it takes to win, no matter what happens. And that mindset helped propel them to Super Bowl XLI. Hopefully this will do the same, especially since it's the first time the Bears have won a game with a -3 turnover differential since then. We'll look back on this game with fond memories when the Bears are gunning for a title. 2. Caleb Williams had his worst game in 2 years This was a game we've quite literally never seen from Williams.

Their latest win also gave the team every reason to believe it can compete with the best in the NFL. Jeffery Simmons made that confidence clear after Sunday’s 27-24 thriller. The defensive tackle took to his X, formerly Twitter, account and shared a powerful message embracing his new team and its growing momentum. Simmons joined Chicago in a blockbuster trade with the Tennessee Titans in late October. The Bears sent two first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round selection to Tennessee for the four-time Pro Bowler and a 2028 fifth-round pick. item.title: Harry Kane left out of FIFPRO World 11 team as Messi returns
item.description: Harry Kane left out of FIFPRO World 11 team as Messi returns Lionel Messi has extended his record number of FIFPRO World 11 appearances to 18, while Lucy Bronze has set a new women’s record after being selected for the ninth time. More than 26,000 professional footballers from 75 countries voted for the 2026 men’s and women’s teams. Messi returns to the team for the first time since 2023 and is joined in the men’s XI by the likes of Erling Haaland, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Though there is no place for Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane. Yamal has also made history by becoming the first player to earn two World 11 selections before turning 20. Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is selected after helping Spain win the 2026 World Cup, with compatriots Pau Cubarsi and Rodri also included. Jude Bellingham is the only English player in the men’s side, while Paris Saint-Germain trio Achraf Hakimi, Nuno Mendes and Vitinha are all recognised. In the women’s team, Bronze makes a record ninth appearance and is one of five England players selected. Chelsea goalkeeper Hannah Hampton, Manchester City defender Alex Greenwood, Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone and Arsenal striker Alessia Russo also make the XI. Barbra Banda is the only player in the women’s team from outside England or Spain, with the Zambia forward earning her third selection. 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11 Goalkeeper: David Raya (Arsenal, Spain) Defenders: Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona, Spain), Achraf Hakimi (Paris Saint-Germain, Morocco), Nuno Mendes (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Midfielders: Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid, England), Rodri (Manchester City/Barcelona, Spain), Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Forwards: Erling Haaland (Manchester City, Norway), Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid, France), Lionel Messi (Inter Miami, Argentina), Lamine Yamal (Barcelona, Spain) 2026 FIFPRO Women’s World 11 Goalkeeper: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea, England) Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea, England), Alex Greenwood (Manchester City, England), Mapi Leon (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain), Irene Paredes (Barcelona, Spain) Midfielders: Aitana Bonmati (Barcelona, Spain), Alexia Putellas (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain), Ella Toone (Manchester United, England) Forwards: Barbra Banda (Orlando Pride, Zambia), Claudia Pina (Barcelona, Spain), Alessia Russo (Arsenal, England) The men’s voting was based on performances between August 4, 2025 and July 19, 2026, while the women’s voting period ran until August 16. Players selected the three footballers they believed had performed best in each position, with the highest-ranked players forming the final World 11.

item.title: Dan Campbell Has Complicated Decision to Make Before Germany Game
item.description: The Detroit Lions improved to 6-2 with Sunday’s 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins, but head coach Dan Campbell now has an interesting decision to make regarding his offensive line. And based on what happened in Miami, it might be a decision that is easier to make on paper than in the locker room. Christian Mahogany was surprisingly benched for violating team rules, opening the door for second-year offensive lineman Miles Frazier to make his first NFL start at left guard. Unfortunately for Detroit, the results weren’t exactly encouraging. Campbell has built his program around accountability, and that’s not something he should abandon. However, with the Lions preparing for another important matchup against the New England Patriots, the question becomes whether Mahogany has already served his punishment or whether Campbell intends to make a longer-term change. His 48.8 pass-blocking grade and team-worst 37.8 run-blocking grade certainly won’t help his argument for remaining in the starting lineup. Frazier played all 59 offensive snaps against Miami, while Mahogany played exclusively on special teams. The Lions also struggled offensively, producing a season-low 270 total yards while Jared Goff was sacked three times. Of course, it would be unfair to blame Detroit’s offensive struggles entirely on Frazier. The offensive line had multiple issues, and Frazier did appear to settle down as the game progressed. However, the numbers make one thing clear: Frazier did not do enough in his first start to make the decision at left guard an obvious one. Dan Campbell Must Balance Discipline With Winning Following Sunday’s victory, Campbell made it clear that Mahogany’s benching was related to team rules rather than simply his performance on the field. item.title: ‘There was some deli meat given out’: Tom Brady takes jab at Drake Maye
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Tom Brady returned to Foxboro this weekend for Rob Gronkowski’s New England Patriots Hall of Fame induction Saturday and Sunday’s game between the Pats and the Green Bay Packers. The former event went swimmingly for New England fans; the latter less so. Led by Jordan Love’s 372 passing yards and four total touchdowns, the Packers routed the Patriots 45-27. Drake Maye, New England’s third-year quarterback, had his share of struggles, tossing three critical interceptions. After the game, Brady the broadcaster had some fun at Maye’s expense during FOX’s postgame interviews. Drake throwing ‘deli meat’ Speaking with Green Bay Packers safety Evan Williams (five tackles, one interception), Brady noted that Maye was being generous with his passes throughout the game. “Xavier [McKinney] had two picks, you had one on the sideline. There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today,” Brady said . “I’m not gonna say that,” Williams responded, laughing, “but he was giving us some gifts for sure.” “There was a few out there, and you made him pay,” Brady added. Tom Brady took a dig at Drake Maye while interviewing #Packers S Evan Williams: “There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today.” ( @NFLonFOX) https://t.co/qp4SfQj1qP — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 9, 2026 If you’re unfamiliar, Brady’s “deli meat” reference is a nod to Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake, who said last week that struggling Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was “throwing deli meat out there” in a loss to the Rams. Lake later apologized to Herbert via text message, claiming he wasn’t trying to be “disrespectful.” Back to Brady We’re guessing Brady wasn’t trying to be cruel toward Maye with his postgame barb, even if his assessment was harsh (though not unfair). After throwing only four touchdowns and seven interceptions in his first four games, Maye tossed 11 TDs and only one pick his next four before Sunday’s ugly showing. “We haven’t had a clean, a turnover-free game yet. It’s, starting with me, it’s one of the biggest differences between winning and losing football games,” Maye said after yesterday’s loss. “I’d say, put our defense in a bad spot in the first, the first drive, and just gave them the football and had some other chances down the field and got to see in front. I got to see in front. I feel like I was just a little late sometimes. I feel like we got into a throwing game, and that’s partly because of what we did offensively, and then we didn’t really get to build off the run game, and I think we just got to start the game, and me specifically, start better.” New England is back in action this Sunday when they take on the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany. item.title: 21 carries expose a Giants rushing plan that needs work
item.description: Nov 8, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; New York Giants running back Devin Singletary (26) runs the ball against Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. (54) during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants won in Philadelphia, but giving Devin Singletary the same workload in the same way is not a complete answer to their running-game problems. Singletary carried 21 times for 31 yards in the 19-11 victory, while the Eagles recorded 14 tackles for loss and six sacks. With Cam Skattebo unavailable for the game, New York leaned heavily on its veteran back and found very little room. The Giants should change the rushing menu The official box score shows Singletary’s longest carry went for 12 yards. Subtracting that play leaves 19 yards on his other 20 attempts. The split does not assign individual blame, but it shows how consistently Philadelphia disrupted the plan. item.title: No room for Kane! Messi back in FIFPRO XI as Yamal breaks teenage record
item.description: Inter Miami CF v Charlotte FC - Getty Images Sport The 2026 FIFPRO Men's World 11 has been officially announced, featuring a mix of legendary veterans and record-breaking youngsters. However, the selection has sparked debate following the high-profile exclusion of Harry Kane, despite the England striker holding the 2026 Ballon d'Or. Messi returns as Yamal makes history Lionel Messi has secured his place in the FIFPRO Men's World 11 once again, marking a triumphant return to the elite lineup for the first time since 2023. His comeback follows a stellar international campaign where he scored eight goals to lead Argentina to the World Cup final, which they narrowly lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time. Joining him in the history books is Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal, who continues to shatter expectations . The Spanish international has become the first player ever to be selected for the World 11 twice before reaching the age of 20. He is one of four Spanish players included in this season's lineup, alongside David Raya, Pau Cubarsi, and Rodri Hernandez. Shock omission for Harry Kane The biggest talking point of the announcement is undoubtedly the absence of Kane. Despite the England captain being the reigning Ballon d'Or winner , he failed to garner enough votes from his fellow professionals to make the final cut. Kane's exclusion highlights the intense competition for attacking spots, with voters clearly favouring a standout frontline. Erling Haaland secured his place after finishing as the Premier League top scorer last season with 27 goals, while also scoring seven times to lead Norway to their first-ever World Cup quarter-final. Alongside him, Kylian Mbappe earned his spot after bagging 10 goals to finish as the World Cup top scorer, officially becoming the tournament's all-time leading goalscorer. Ligue 1 and PSG dominance Paris Saint-Germain enjoyed a strong showing in the final XI, with the French champions boasting three representatives in the squad following their back-to-back Champions League titles. The defensive unit features Moroccan star Achraf Hakimi and Portuguese left-back Nuno Mendes, alongside midfielder Vitinha, all rewarded for their pivotal roles in the club's European success. The lineup was selected following a vote by 19,806 professional footballers across 73 countries. Eligible players were evaluated on their performances between August 4, 2025, and July 19, 2026, provided they featured in at least 30 official matches during that period. The complete 2026 FIFPro World 11 The complete 2026 FIFPro World 11 lineup features Raya in goal, behind a backline of Hakimi, Cubarsi, and Mendes. The midfield trio consists of Rodri, Vitinha, and Jude Bellingham, while Messi, Yamal, Mbappe, and Haaland form a formidable frontline.
